text:
ellen.sales: Hey team — CorpX sec questionnaire back. Two asks we need answers for ASAP: 1) they want to know the recommended topology for isolation (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) for an LLM private deploy POC. 2) firewall rules / exact ports & egress IPs for their security team. Also pricing: they asked how egress billing works if we route through a proxy vs interface endpoint.

raj.platform: For isolation: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is preferred when customers want to avoid cross-account peering and restrict traffic to a managed endpoint. Peering is simpler for intra-org VPCs but leaks routing. If they need strict allowlisting + no route exposure -> PrivateLink.

morgan.network: +1 on PrivateLink for POC. If they use our connector inside their VPC, traffic goes out via an interface endpoint to Redwood private service. From firewall perspective, they only need outbound TLS to the interface endpoint IPs we provide. No peering routes required.

ellen.sales: Good. They also asked for exact ports and protocols to include in their questionnaire. Can we paste a concise snippet I can give to their security team?

alex.engineer: Sure — minimal rules we recommend for PrivateLink + connector: 
```
Outbound rules from customer subnet to interface endpoint IPs (AWS):
- TCP 443 to <InterfaceEndpointIPs> (TLS, gRPC/HTTPS)
- UDP 123 to NTP if they require time sync (optional)
- TCP 443 to our healthcheck endpoints for SaaS control-plane (if using hosted)
```
Also note: if they terminate TLS on a proxy (TLS inspect), session pinning will break our mutual TLS for connector auth — recommend allowing passthrough or using a TLS-inspecting proxy that preserves SNI.

morgan.network: Add firewall note: if they use an egress proxy for all outbound, we need outbound source NAT preserved if they expect per-tenant src-IP preservation. Otherwise traffic appears from proxy IPs. For PrivateLink, we give explicit endpoint IPs to allowlist on their firewall.

tim.security: For the questionnaire: they asked about key management and compliance. Short answers: we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments (bring-your-own), we provide SOC2 attestation docs, and we can provide network diagrams showing no peering routes when using PrivateLink. I'll attach doc links when I have them.

ellen.sales: Pricing q: customer asked whether routing via their existing egress proxy (so we don't use interface endpoint) would incur additional egress charges on our side or theirs. Raj?

raj.platform: Billing-wise: Hosted API egress billed per-token/response per their account usage; Private deployments pricing varies — if traffic leaves their VPC to our managed service, cloud egress charges might apply on their cloud bill (standard AWS data transfer). If they keep traffic in-region via PrivateLink, there are interface endpoint charges (customer's account) but less public egress. For Dedicated/Private contract, we can include estimated data transfer in the quote.

ellen.sales: Can you provide a short line I can paste into RFP about network impact and cost tradeoffs?

raj.platform: Paste-ready: "Recommended: use PrivateLink interface endpoints for isolated POC traffic. This eliminates cross-account peering and minimizes public egress. AWS interface endpoint hourly and per-GB charges apply to the customer's account; Redwood's hosted pricing remains usage-based. For Dedicated/Private deployments, data transfer can be included in the reserved contract—ask solutions for an egress-inclusive quote."

ellen.sales: Perfect. Security wants a snippet for the questionnaire about allowed IPs and how to validate endpoints.

alex.engineer: Add this snippet: 
```
IP allowlist and validation:
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to provided interface endpoint IPs (we'll supply 3-5 per region)
- Use TLS SNI and certificate pinning to validate Redwood service certs
- Optional: mTLS for connector auth (Private deploy); we provide certs and CA details during onboarding
```

morgan.network: One more operational note: for high-throughput tests (LLM inference), recommend opening bandwidth to endpoint subnets and testing with burst policy. If they use NAT gateway egress, ensure SNAT port exhaustion isn't hit for many concurrent connections (we can share load guidelines).

ellen.sales: Ok I'll send: 1) topology recommendation (PrivateLink), 2) firewall rules + code snippets, 3) pricing blurb, 4) compliance bullets from Tim. Tim pls attach SOC2/KMS links.

tim.security: Will attach SOC2, ISO, and KMS integration guide to the thread by EOD. Also: if the customer wants an ATO-style network diagram, we have a template — I can generate it for CorpX if we get a contact.

tim.security: Will attach SOC2, ISO, and KMS integration guide to the thread by EOD. Also: if the customer wants an ATO-style network diagram, we have a template — I can generate it for CorpX if we get a contact.

ellen.sales: Thanks all. @sre-bot can you post the interface endpoint IP list once we provision the POC?

sre-bot: Sure — I'll post the autogenerated endpoint IPs when the infra ticket (INF-7892) finishes provisioning. (reaction :white_check_mark:)

ellen.sales: Great — sending email to customer now. Will follow up with attachments and the FAQ snippet. :thumbsup:
